title: The Salt of the Sundered Sea
premise: Wendell Eastwick has spent twelve years hiding her gatekeeper's blood beneath a shopkeeper's apron in Greyharbor, a city that drowned its mages and outlawed magic. When a dying courier presses a salt-stained map into her hands, Wendell learns the Sundered Sea is tearing open, and the covenant her family once forged between realms is failing because she alone can reforge it. Hunted by the Ministry of Unmaking and shadowed by a smuggler crew who become the family she never had, she must sail to the drowned gate and choose between sealing it forever—killing the sea-folk who sheltered her mother—or paying the price of survival herself. In the end, Wendell reforges the covenant with her own name written into it, trading her invisibility for a life bound to both worlds.
about_author: Mirabel Thackeray is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who grew up on stories of drowned kingdoms and stubborn women. She writes fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked for, from a coastal cottage full of maps and cats.

chapters.title: The Shop That Sold Nothing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet Greyharbor's charm market, where Wendell sells harmless trinkets while concealing the faint hum of the sealed gate beneath her cellar. A routine inspection by the Ministry nearly exposes her. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a woman pretending to be ordinary.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A stranger collapses at her door at low tide, bleeding brine instead of blood, and presses a map etched on fish-skin into her hands with the words 'the Eastwick debt comes due.' He dies before dawn; Ministry investigators arrive by morning. Emotional beat: dread—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with first appearance of Captain Isolde Vane's crew. To follow the map out of the harbor, Wendell trades her last hidden charm for passage aboard the Kestrel's Tooth. The crew is suspicious, half-feral, oddly loyal. Emotional beat: reluctant trust offered under duress.

chapters.title: What the Tide Remembers
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. At sea, the map reveals itself only when touched by gatekeeper's blood, forcing Wendell to confess her lineage. Isolde reveals her own stake: her brother was taken by the sea-folk years ago. Emotional beat: two guarded women recognizing each other's wounds.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The ship crosses into waters where the Sundered Sea bleeds through—a shimmering rift where drowned voices sing. A sea-child surfaces and calls Wendell by her mother's name. Emotional beat: wonder tangled with grief; the magic she buried is beautiful after all.

chapters.title: Ministry of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs: Inspector Corvane hunts the Kestrel's Tooth, while back home Wendell's apprentice is interrogated. The crew learns the Ministry doesn't want the gate closed—it wants the covenant broken so Greyharbor can harvest the other realm. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own homeland.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The sea-folk reveal the covenant's terms: it must be reforged by an Eastwick, and the price is a life freely given. Isolde offers herself for her brother; Wendell refuses to let another pay for her inheritance. First quarrel, then first real bond. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other over survival logic.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Gate
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Ministry fleet corners them at the drowned gate; the Kestrel's Tooth burns; the crew fights so Wendell can reach the threshold. Isolde is gravely wounded shielding her. Emotional beat: terror and fury—the cost of being loved made visible.

chapters.title: Covenant of Salt and Name
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, climax. Within the gate, she faces the covenant's guardian and the ghost-memory of her mother, who chose secrecy and doomed the realms. Wendell writes her own name into the covenant—not as sacrifice but as stewardship, binding herself to both shores. The rift steadies; the Ministry's claim dissolves. Emotional beat: claiming inheritance on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Two Shores
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating Wendell and Isolde. Months later, Greyharbor's law has cracked; Wendell reopens her shop openly, now a bridge between realms, with the sea-child as her apprentice and Isolde recovering above the cellar gate. The crew gathers for supper. Emotional beat: quiet joy—an invisible woman finally seen, surrounded by family she chose.
